After a long and hard day at work, many people look forward to a good meal, preferably comfort food. In Philippines, that arguably equates to home-grown Jollibee, which has become synonymous to Filipino identity, especially abroad.
That was apparently the train of thought of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. when United States President Donald Trump was in town for a brief state visit.
In his opening remarks during his bilateral meeting with Trump on Wednesday, November 18, Marcos acknowledged the US leader’s tight schedule in the Philippines. Trump arrived late Tuesday afternoon, November 17, and headed straight to the Philippine International Convention Center to attend the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue meeting , the ASEAN-US Special Summit , and other meetings after the conclusion of the 49th ASEAN Summit.
“Your schedule has been packed to the hilt, which is not exactly a surprise because we know how hard you work,” Marcos told Trump.
The Philippine leader said this was why he decided to at least give Trump and his delegation a “taste of Manila” and had Jollibee snacks delivered to them.
“Jollibee is a very very popular chain, and one of their main products is fried chicken, and we are very proud to say that we have surpassed KFC in the United States in terms of popularity,” Marcos said.
“You have been working very hard, Mr. President….So just think of it as providing extra energy for all the work that you have to do, that you have done, and continue to do, and that is in front of you,” Marcos said.
Diplomacy via Jollibee is nothing new. In July, Marcos and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney paid a visit to a Jollibee store in Vancouver following their bilateral meeting.
The company is operating over 100 stores in North America and plans to reach 500 stores by 2030. (READ: How Jollibee became Filipino food’s biggest ambassador in the US )
In the recently concluded 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit and Related Summits, the Jollibee mascot, wearing a barong, made an appearance at the International Media Center , located at the World Trade Center in Pasay City on Tuesday.
That’s days after Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese sampled Chickenjoy and announced that the food chain will also open its doors across New South Wales and Victoria .
“Its establishment in Australia will answer the diaspora’s calls to make home-style Filipino dishes more accessible and provide an opportunity for Australians to experience Filipino cuisine and culture firsthand,” according to a news release from Albanese’s website.
As for the late night Jollibee delivery to Trump, well, it just showed how Marcos cared for his “very, very important guest.” Bida ang saya nga naman! – Rappler.com
